prompt: How has Falcon (FALC) been doing on velocity and say/do over its recent sprints? I'm trying to decide how much to commit for next sprint.
final_text:
Falcon finishes about **32 story points a sprint on average (range 21–40)**, but finishes only **about 79% of what it commits to**. For next sprint I'd suggest committing **about 28–30 points (roughly 9–10 items)**, plus a stretch item or two.

These figures cover Falcon's last 6 standard sprints, 2026.18 through 2026.24 (July 8 to October 13). Sprint 2026.23 is left out because it was an innovation and planning sprint, not a normal one.

| Measure | Average | Range |
|---|---|---|
| Velocity (story points) | 31.8 | 21–40 |
| Velocity (items) | 10.5 | 8–13 |
| Predictability (points) | 88% | 65–100% |
| Say/do (points) | 79% | 57–94% |

**By sprint (story points):**

| Sprint | Velocity | Predictability | Say/do |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.24 (latest) | 34 | 95% | 85% |
| 2026.22 | 27 | 78% | 66% |
| 2026.21 | 38 | 100% | 92% |
| 2026.20 | 21 | 65% | 57% |
| 2026.19 | 31 | 89% | 80% |
| 2026.18 | 40 | 100% | 94% |

**What this means for the commitment:**
- **Falcon commits more than it finishes.** Working back from the numbers, the team has committed about 32–36 points most sprints. Predictability (88%) is higher than say/do (79%) because finished work added mid-sprint covers for committed work left undone. Of the committed work itself, the team has finished somewhere between about 18 and 31 points a sprint.
- **The results swing between sprints.** Strong sprints (38–40 points) alternate with weak ones (21–27). The 32-point average sits close to the top of that range, so it's a risky number to commit to.
- **The latest sprint was good** (34 points, 85% say/do), but one sprint isn't enough to call it a trend.

Committing about 28–30 points puts you a bit under the average. On recent results, the team would then finish most or all of its commitment in most sprints, and a stretch item gives you a way to use the extra capacity in a strong sprint. If you know of something unusual next sprint, like time off or a large unplanned piece of work, lower the number to match.

If it helps, I can also run a throughput forecast for Falcon's backlog to see which items it's likely to finish by the end of next sprint.

prompt: Where did the Raptors put their effort between July 1 and September 30, 2026? Break it down by project.
final_text:
The biggest single share of the Raptors' effort from July 1 to September 30, 2026 went to work linked to no project: about a third (32.7%). Of the work that was linked to a project, Mobile Experience Refresh took the most.

Over the quarter the three teams finished 412 work items. All four projects belong to the Digital Commerce portfolio, and none of them is in a program.

| Project | Share of effort | Items | Team that did the most |
|---|---|---|---|
| **No project** | **32.7%** | 135 | Kestrel (82 items) |
| Mobile Experience Refresh (MOBX) | 26.4% | 109 | Osprey (87 items) |
| Payments Reconciliation (PAYRC) | 18.9% | 78 | Kestrel (62 items) |
| Self-Service Onboarding (ONBRD) | 15.2% | 63 | Falcon (50 items) |
| Billing Export Retirement (BILLX) | 6.8% | 28 | Falcon (22 items) |

**Notes:**
- **The work with no project is the main finding.** About a third of the group's effort can't be traced to any project, which is well above the 20–30% range where it starts to hide a lot of work from portfolio reporting. Kestrel did most of it: 82 of those 135 items, which is over half of Kestrel's 141 completed items. It's worth asking Kestrel what that work was, such as support, technical debt or unplanned requests, and whether some of it should be linked to Payments Reconciliation or another project.
- **Each team leans toward one project.** Osprey did most of its project work on Mobile Experience Refresh. Kestrel did Payments Reconciliation, and Falcon split its project work between Self-Service Onboarding and Billing Export Retirement.
- **The work was spread evenly across teams:** Falcon 34.2%, Kestrel 34.2%, Osprey 31.6%.
- **How effort is measured:** each team's work is measured in its own sizing method, and the teams are combined by their share of completed items. This avoids adding up story points that teams estimate on different scales. Among the teams that size in story points, 248 of 271 items had an estimate.

I asked for a 180-day window instead, but the response still came back using 90 days, so the longer window didn't take effect.

**My own rough estimate, not Wayd's figure:** 7 items in about 13 weeks is roughly 0.5 items a week. At that pace the 18 open items would last about 33 weeks. Seven items is too few to plan on, though, so treat that as a loose guess. If it's anywhere near right, the backlog is long rather than short. Wayd flags anything over 26 weeks as At Risk.

**Is the backlog ready to plan a PI from? Not yet.** These are the problems, using Wayd's default thresholds:

**The healthy parts:** nothing is old and still proposed, there's no work carried over, and no active work is unassigned. Aging WIP and Oversized couldn't be assessed, for the same reason as Runway.

**Also worth checking:** Wayd grades WIP Load Healthy at 1 active item per member, but all 6 In Progress items are assigned to Marcus Hale. If that reflects how work is really split, it's a bottleneck.

**Before planning:**
